definition: Sebastian Thrun (born May 14, 1967) is a German-American computer scientist, entrepreneur, and educator.
details: He is an adjunct professor at Stanford University and is known for his work in self-driving cars, robotics, artificial intelligence, and online education. He is the co-founder of Google X, co-founder of Udacity, and former chief executive officer of Kitty Hawk Corporation. He is widely recognized for his contributions to autonomous driving systems, particularly as leader of the Google Chauffeur Project (now known as Waymo) and as the leader of the Stanford Racing that won the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge, an event widely credited with accelerating research in self-driving technology.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is Sebastian Thrun — a small key that opens a big door.
